title: Where Starship should land
method: Every 0.125 degree cell between -60 and 60 degrees latitude (about 7 km) gets four checks from public orbital data: ice within reach and low ground from SpaceX's stated criteria, plume-safe ground and science reach from us. Each check is go, watch or no-go with a 0 to 1 goodness; a cell's status is its worst check, the same rule as a farm's flag on Earth; the score is the weighted mean of goodness (ice 0.35, low_elevation 0.20, plume_safe_ground 0.25, science_reach 0.20). Sunlight, latitude and landing-scale rock hazards are shown but not scored: SpaceX screens for them and HiRISE is the right tool. Sites are the best go cells at least 300 km apart.

factors.name: Ice within reach
factors.dataset: SWIM ice consistency, 0-1 m and 1-5 m (PSI)
factors.why: Water for propellant, air and crops.

factors.name: Low ground
factors.dataset: MOLA MEGDR elevation, 16 pixels per degree (NASA PDS)
factors.why: More atmosphere to slow the ship.
factors.goodness_rule: 1 at -4,000 m or lower, 0 at +1,000 m or higher, linear between

factors.name: Plume-safe ground
factors.dataset: MGS TES nighttime thermal inertia, 20 pixels per degree (Putzig and Mellon, PSI)
factors.why: Firm soil the engines will not dig out: very low inertia is loose dust, very high is rock and bedrock.

factors.name: Science reach
factors.dataset: USGS Mars Global Geologic Map, SIM 3292 (Tanaka et al. 2014)
factors.why: More kinds of rock within a rover's range, and rock from the wet early eras.
factors.go: >= 4 distinct units within about 100 km, including a Noachian or Hesperian one
factors.goodness_rule: 0.7 x min(1, units / 6) + 0.3 x (1 if an old unit is within reach else 0)

shown_not_scored.name: Regional slope
shown_not_scored.why: Flat, rock-free ground is SpaceX's own screen and needs HiRISE at landing scale; a 20 km slope is context, not a verdict.

shown_not_scored.name: Latitude
shown_not_scored.why: Sunlight and power are SpaceX's own screen (within about 40 degrees of the equator); we show it and leave it to them.

shown_not_scored.name: Dust (albedo)
shown_not_scored.why: Bright ground usually means a dust cover; thermal inertia already scores the firmness, so albedo stays context.

blind_spots: no sunlight or power factor (SpaceX screens for it; we leave it to them)
no rock-hazard factor at landing scale (HiRISE work)
7 km cells are far coarser than a landing ellipse
SWIM covers 60 S to 60 N only
thermal inertia is a regional average; local boulders are invisible at this scale
about 15 percent of the thermal inertia map between 60 S and 60 N is the authors' interpolated fill (TES mask); those cells are flagged in the detail text

spacex_summary: Of SpaceX's 6 2019 sites, 1 lands in the go band, 4 in watch and 1 in no-go on our screen: all 6 pass the ice check; all 6 pass the low-ground check; all 6 pass our plume check; 1 of 6 fail our science-reach check.

tradeoff.y: our factors goodness (plume-safe ground and science reach)
